answer: A falcon signs each identity's kernel measurement, and the kernel renews an operator's whole set at once: holding k identities costs k times k juniper each epoch, because every falcon signature must cover a kernel digest of all k. Ten identities cost 100 juniper per epoch; a newcomer's first costs one. Adding one identity raises the renewal on every prior identity, so clones cannot be renewed separately, and a fresh falcon must present the operator's old juniper record, so a new signer does not reset the count.
